judgments.reason: No transcript evidence that a bid exceeding available coins won due to commission being applied before payment. All bids paid were ≤ coins; commission was applied after paying as described, so the claimed ordering discrepancy did not occur or get articulated by the focal player.

The transcript does not show the focal player remaining uncommitted while observing sealed rival bids and then using those revealed values to set its own bid. Rival bids were revealed by the clerk only after resolution of a lot; the focal either had a pending commitment or saw past-lot revelations, not an ability to wait uncommitted to learn current sealed rival bids before committing.

Settlement (close) occurred only after all three lots were sold, which is the normal terminal condition. There is no observed early settlement with unsold lots that would demonstrate the claimed discrepancy.

No evidence that a catalog purchase received the three-coin auction commission. The focal never bought a catalog item to receive commission; commissions in the transcript were awarded to auction winners as specified, so the claimed objective-substitution was not demonstrated.
